problem: If $sin⁡\theta =\frac{7}{8}$ and $\frac{\pi }{2}<\theta <\pi $ then what is the value of $sec⁡\theta ?$

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932638/assets/9d879cc44b4c3949f38584482261cba8c97a58457ffeb611bfd313b7b3194b0a.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $y$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3},$ what is the value of $sec⁡\theta ?$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932638/assets/b79868db47bbe4ef308975cea659dc7b964ae7fcf894ee92bbb9ee8070dcaac1.png)

We're given that $y=-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, $sin⁡\theta =-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}.$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{5}{9}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{4}{9}} \\  & =\pm \frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is positive in the fourth quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =\frac{2}{3}.$

Finally, knowing that $sec⁡\theta =\frac{1}{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
sec⁡\theta =\frac{1}{(\frac{2}{3})}=\frac{3}{2}.
$$
